question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'** i.e.** 'Slightly'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **most appropriate option **to fill in blank number 1 is:** "slightly"**
 
• The term **"slightly"** is an adverb that modifies the adjective "alkaline," meaning that the saliva is a little or to a small degree alkaline.
 
• This makes sense in the context, as saliva is indeed slightly alkaline.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *'The thought here is that because saliva is **slightly** alkaline, stimulating it by chewing gum after eating (2)______ help neutralize the acidity in your mouth and throat. (3)________ a very small study from 2005 did (4)_______ some merit to this approach, the size of the study makes it difficult to (5)_______ any real conclusions.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options aren't correct:
 
 
• **"Slight"** is an adjective that means small in degree or inconsiderable, and it doesn't grammatically fit here as we need an adverb to modify the adjective "alkaline."
 
• **"Slightest" **is the superlative form of the adjective "slight," meaning the smallest or least degree. However, in this sentence, we need an adverb to modify the adjective "alkaline."
 
• **"Slighter" **is the comparative form of the adjective "slight," meaning lesser or smaller in amount, extent, or degree. However, in this sentence, we need an adverb to modify the adjective "alkaline."
